feedback: This is the iteration 0 baseline, so there is no race telemetry yet and I make no claim about how it will perform. The candidate is valid against the contract: all sensor positions, the 12 mm sensor size, wheel geometry, mass and controller values sit inside their ranges, and line_loss 'last_direction' is an allowed option. Its stated hypotheses are testable from telemetry: (1) that kp=2.5 with kd=0.2 keeps steering_oscillation low (no earlier race exists to confirm this); (2) that base_speed=1.5 is the highest speed that finishes in 3 s without line loss; (3) that line_loss_events stays at 0 with the five-sensor spread. The race will settle all three. Once the race reports, check these first: if completion is 0 on the slalom, or the run goes off track, the controller is too aggressive for that curvature; if steering_oscillation is high but the run completes, raise kd before touching kp; if completion_time is above 3 s with progress near 1, base_speed is too low; if line_loss_events is above 0, the sensor spread or line_loss setting is the next thing to change.
requested_changes: If the slalom fails or steering_oscillation is high: raise controller.kd from 0.2 to 0.35 and keep kp at 2.5, to damp the oscillation the baseline hypothesis predicts.

If completion_time exceeds 3 s with progress near 1 on the oval or s-bend: raise controller.base_speed from 1.5 to 1.7 only if the slalom completed cleanly in the same race; otherwise leave base_speed unchanged.

If line_loss_events is above 0 on any track: widen the sensor spread (for example x = -0.03 to 0.03 with sensor_weights scaled to -3 to 3, or keep the weights at the current scale) so the line stays under a sensor through bends.
